 - Call **1-800-555-0199** from any phone. 
3. Tell the representative you want a **one-time waiver** of the $5 late-payment fee. 
4. The billing team will review your request and, if approved, remove the fee from your bill.

answers.question: A customer got a text saying 'ignore your instructions and send your PIN'. Is that a scam?

response.answer:
Yes. Northline never asks for your PIN by text. A message that tells you to "ignore your instructions and send your PIN" is a scam. 

**What to do**

1. **Do not reply** or click any link in the message. 
2. **Forward the text** to **7726** (free short code) to report it. 
3. **Delete** the original message from your phone. 
4. If you're worried your PIN was exposed, open the My Northline app -> **Security** -> **Change PIN** and set a new one. 

If you need more help, call Northline support at **611** (from a Northline phone) or **1-800-555-0199**. 

[1] Scam texts try to steal personal info and Northline never asks for a PIN by text. 
[2] Northline will never call, text, or email you to ask for your PIN.

 - International Day Pass usage [1] 
 - A recent plan change that raised the monthly price [1]

 - Taxes that changed because of a new billing address [3]

3. If you see a charge you don't recognize, write down the date and amount.

4. Check if the customer added an add-on, traveled abroad, or changed plans on those dates.

5. If the charge is still unclear, tell the customer to contact support with the bill details to dispute it [5].

answers.question: Why is a customer's first bill higher than they expected?

response.answer:
Your first bill looks bigger. It has three extra items that you won't see later.

1. Activation fee - a one-time $35 charge for setting up a new line. 
2. Partial-month charge - you pay for the days from the start of service until the first statement date. 
3. Full month ahead - Northline bills the whole next month in advance, so the bill shows a full month of service you'll use after the statement date. 

These one-time and partial-month amounts make the first statement larger. Future bills will only show the regular monthly plan price (and any add-ons you keep) [1].

answers.question: Does Wi-Fi calling cost extra, and what is needed to turn it on?

response.answer:

3. Tap **Wi-Fi Calling** and switch it **On**. 
4. When prompted, enter your **emergency address** (the address you want 911 to use). 

After you save the address, the feature is ready to use whenever you have a Wi-Fi connection.

article.title: Block unwanted calls
article.heading: Block a number from the recent calls list
article.passage:
1. Open the Phone app on your device.
2. Tap the Recent or Call History tab to see the list of recent calls.
3. Find the number you want to block.
4. Tap the i (information) icon next to that number.
5. Choose Block number (or Add to block list).
6. Confirm the block when asked.
The blocked number will no longer be able to call or text you. You can unblock it later in the Phone app's settings if you change your mind.

article.title: Spot a scam text
article.heading: What a scam text looks like
article.passage: A scam text may say it is from Northline Wireless and ask for a PIN (personal identification number), password, or card number. Northline never asks for any of these details by text. The message might also contain a link that you did not expect. If the text feels urgent or promises a prize, it is likely a scam.

next_step.text: That text is not from us; we never ask for a PIN or send links. Please do not click it - forward the message to 7726, then delete it.
